newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures finish mixed in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures finish mixed in quiet trading.

text.p: U.S. debt futures finished mixed in very quiet trading, with June Treasury bonds lower and near session lows.

June poked above resistance at last week's high of 107-26/32 and reached 107-28/32, but eroded for the rest of the day. Traders said that failure scared bulls back to the sidelines and left the market vulnerable to weak technical factors.
The fundamental line-up was empty today, with most players waiting for Friday's March Retail Sales and Producer Price Index.
Traders tied some afternoon weakness to corporate supply pressure.

"I don't know if the late pressure will be enough to keep this soft tomorrow," one T-bond futures trader said. "We'll have to see tomorrow if claims mean anything or if any of these Fed governors say anything to move the market," he said. The latest weekly jobless claims will be released Thursday at 0730 CDT/1230 GMT, with several Federal Reserve officials speaking at various events across the country Thursday.
Others said consolidation would direct prices.
"We're going to wait until Friday," another trader said.
"Jobless claims are going to have to be drastic either way for this market to do anything tomorrow," a Eurodollar floor source said.
Claims were forecast at 313,000 in the week ended April 5, down from 314,00 in the previous report.
Traders noted that the market has remained largely in a range since the beginning of April, with six session highs from 107-23/32 to 107-28/32 possibly keeping a lid on any more gains.
"This is no man's land that we've been in for a couple of weeks," a bond trader said.
"You've got to get out of there before we really see anything happen," he said. He pegged support at 107-5/32 to 8/32 and resistance at 108-00.

At the close, June T-bonds were down 2/32 at 107-11/32, notes were flat at 105-22/32, munis rose 9/32 to 112-7/32, Sept bills rose 0.005 bps to 94.300, Sept Euros gained 0.005 to 93.725. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
